The {@link Exchange} also holds meta-data during its entire\n    32→ * lifetime stored as properties accessible using the various {@link #getProperty(String)} methods. The\n    33→ * {@link #setProperty(String, Object)} is used to store a property. For example, you can use this to store security,\n    34→ * SLA related data or any other information deemed useful throughout processing. If an {@link Exchange} failed during\n    35→ * routing the {@link Exception} that caused the failure is stored and accessible via the {@link #getException()}\n    36→ * method.\n    37→ * <p/>\n    38→ * An Exchange is created when a {@link Consumer} receives a request. A new {@link Message} is created, the request is\n    39→ * set as the body of the {@link Message} and depending on the {@link Consumer} other {@link Endpoint} and protocol\n    40→ * related information is added as headers on the {@link Message}. Then an Exchange is created and the newly created\n    41→ * {@link Message} is set as the in on the Exchange. Therefore, an Exchange starts its life in a {@link Consumer}. The\n    42→ * Exchange is then sent down the {@link Route} for processing along a {@link Processor} chain. The {@link Processor} as\n    43→ * the name suggests is what processes the {@link Message} in the Exchange and Camel, in addition to providing\n    44→ * out-of-the-box a large number of useful processors, it also allows you to create your own. The rule Camel uses is to\n    45→ * take the out {@link Message} produced by the previous {@link Processor} and set it as the in for the next\n    46→ * {@link Processor}. If the previous {@link Processor} did not produce an out, then the in of the previous\n    47→ * {@link Processor} is sent as the next in. At the end of the processing chain, depending on the {@link ExchangePattern\n    48→ * Message Exchange Pattern} (or MEP) the last out (or in of no out available) is sent by the {@link Consumer} back to\n    49→ * the original caller.\n    50→ * <p/>\n    51→ * Camel, in addition to providing out-of-the-box a large number of useful processors, it also allows you to implement\n    52→ * and use your own. When the Exchange is passed to a {@link Processor}, it always contains an in {@link Message} and no\n    53→ * out {@link Message}. The {@link Processor} <b>may</b> produce an out, depending on the nature of the\n    54→ * {@link Processor}. The in {@link Message} can be accessed using the {@link #getIn()} method. Since the out message is\n    55→ * null when entering the {@link Processor}, the {@link #getOut()} method is actually a convenient factory method that\n    56→ * will lazily instantiate a {@link org.apache.camel.support.DefaultMessage} which you could populate. As an alternative\n    57→ * you could also instantiate your specialized {@link Message} and set it on the exchange using the\n    58→ * {@link #setOut(org.apache.camel.Message)} method. Please note that a {@link Message} contains not only the body but\n    59→ * also headers and attachments. If you are creating a new {@link Message} the headers and attachments of the in\n    60→ * {@link Message} are not automatically copied to the out by Camel, and you'll have to set the headers and attachments\n    61→ * you need yourself. If your {@link Processor} is not producing a different {@link Message} but only needs to slightly\n    62→ * modify the in, you can simply update the in {@link Message} returned by {@link #getIn()}.\n    63→ * <p/>\n    64→ * See this <a href=\"http://camel.apache.org/using-getin-or-getout-methods-on-exchange.html\">FAQ entry</a> for more\n    65→ * details.\n    66→ */\n    67→@ConstantProvider(\"org.apache.camel.ExchangeConstantProvider\")\n    68→public interface Exchange extends VariableAware {\n    69→\n    70→    String AUTHENTICATION = \"CamelAuthentication\";\n    71→    String AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE_POLICY_ID = \"CamelAuthenticationFailurePolicyId\";\n    72→\n    73→    @Metadata(label = \"aggregate\", description = \"Number of exchanges that was grouped together.\", javaType = \"int\",\n    74→              important = true)\n    75→    String AGGREGATED_SIZE = \"CamelAggregatedSize\";\n    76→    @Metadata(label = \"aggregate\", description = \"The time in millis this group will timeout\", javaType = \"long\")\n    77→    String AGGREGATED_TIMEOUT = \"CamelAggregatedTimeout\";\n    78→    @Metadata(label = \"aggregate\", description = \"Enum that tell how this group was completed\",\n    79→              enums = \"consumer,force,interval,predicate,size,strategy,timeout\", javaType = \"String\")\n    80→    String AGGREGATED_COMPLETED_BY = \"CamelAggregatedCompletedBy\";\n    81→    @Metadata(label = \"aggregate\", description = \"The correlation key for this aggregation group\", javaType = \"String\",\n    82→              important = true)\n    83→    String AGGREGATED_CORRELATION_KEY = \"CamelAggregatedCorrelationKey\";\n    84→    String AGGREGATED_COLLECTION_GUARD = \"CamelAggregatedCollectionGuard\";\n    85→    String AGGREGATION_STRATEGY = \"CamelAggregationStrategy\";\n    86→    @Metadata(label = \"consumer,aggregate\",\n    87→              description = \"Input property. re-schedule a new thread\n   300→    }\n   301→\n   302→    /**\n   303→     * No messages to poll so send an empty message instead.\n   304→     *\n   305→     * @throws Exception is thrown if error (isSuspended()) return;\n    \n    // Handle backoff logic\n    if (backoffMultiplier > 0 && \n        (idleCounter >= backoffIdleThreshold || errorCounter >= backoffErrorThreshold)) {\n        if (backoffCounter < backoffMultiplier) {\n            return;  // Skip this poll\n        }\n        // Reset counters\n    }\n    \n    // Check repeat count limit\n    if (repeatCount > 0 && counter > strategy\n                        pollStrategy.commit(this, endpoint, polledMessages);\n                        \n                        // Greedy: keep polling if messages\n          lastError = null;\n                            firstPollDone = true;\n                        }\n                    }\n                } finally {\n                    pollingCounter.decrementAndGet();\n                }\n            }\n        } catch (Exception e) {\n            // Rollback strategy - may retry\n            boolean retry = pollStrategy.rollback(this, endpoint, retryCounter, e);\n            if (!retry) {\n                cause = e;\n                done = true;\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Handle exception\n        if (cause != null && isRunAllowed()) {\n            getExceptionHandler().handleException(\n                \"Failed polling endpoint\", cause);\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // (polledMessages == 0) {\n            idleCounter.incrementAndGet();\n        } else {\n            idleCounter.set(0);\n        }\n        successCounter.incrementAndGet();\n        errorCounter.set(0);\n        lastError = null;\n    }\n    \n    firstPollDone = true;\n}\n```\n\n**Abstract Methods:**\n```java\nprotected abstract int poll() throws Exception;  // Must return Component (DefaultComponent)\n   ├─ URI: \"kafka:topic?brokers=localhost:9092\"\n   └─ createEndpoint(uri, parameters)\n      ├─ Parse URI → path=\"topic\", query params\n      ├─ Validate URI syntax and parameters\n      └─ Call abstract createEndpoint(uri, path, params)\n         └─ Component implementation creates endpoint\n   \n2. Endpoint (DefaultEndpoint or subclass)\n   ├─ Stores URI, ExchangePattern, exception handling config\n   │\n   └─ When route attaches consumer:\n      ├─ createConsumer(Processor processor)\n      │  └─ Component implementation creates consumer instance\n      │     └─ Passes processor (the route/pipeline) to consumer\n      │\n      └─ When route uses producer:\n         ├─ createProducer() or createAsyncProducer()\n         └─ Returns producer wrapping any processor/executor\n\n3. Consumer (DefaultConsumer or ScheduledPollConsumer)\n   ├─ Stores:\n   │  ├─ endpoint (back-reference)\n   │  ├─ processor (the ROUTE - the pipeline to execute)\n   │  ├─ asyncProcessor (async wrapper of processor)\n   │  └─ exchangeFactory (for pooling)\n   │\n   └─ When message arrives:\n      ├─ createExchange() → uses exchangeFactory\n      ├─ endpoint.configureExchange(exchange)\n      ├─ getAsyncProcessor().process(exchange, callback)\n      │  └─ Processor (route) processes the exchange\n      └─ Callback returns exchange to pool\n\n4. Producer (DefaultProducer or DefaultAsyncProducer)\n   ├─ Stores: endpoint\n   │\n   └─ When message sent:\n      └─ process(Exchange) → Send to endpoint's target system\n\n5. ScheduledPollConsumer (extends DefaultConsumer + Runnable)\n   ├─ Same as DefaultConsumer, but:\n   │\n   ├─ Has ScheduledExecutorService\n   ├─ run() method called on schedule\n   └─ doRun() → poll() → process each message via processor\n```\n\n---\n\n### **Key Design Patterns**\n\n1. **Service Lifecycle Pattern:** All use `ServiceSupport` with `doInit/doBuild/doStart/doStop/doShutdown`\n\n2. **Async/Sync Duality:**\n   - `DefaultProducer` (sync) → `process(Exchange)`\n   - `DefaultAsyncProducer` (async) → `process(Exchange, AsyncCallback)`\n   - `AsyncProcessorConverterHelper` bridges them\n\n3. **Processor Injection:**\n   - Consumer gets Processor in constructor (the route pipeline)\n   - Processor execution handles routing/error handling\n   - Async callback returns control when done\n\n4. **Exchange Factory Pattern:**\n   - Each consumer gets dedicated `ExchangeFactory` \n   - Enables pooling/reuse of Exchange objects\n   - Per-consumer isolation\n\n5. **Strategy Pattern:**\n   - `PollingConsumerPollStrategy` for begin/commit/rollback hooks\n   - `ScheduledPollConsumerScheduler` for scheduling implementation\n   - `ExceptionHandler` for error handling\n\n6. **PropertyConfigurer Pattern:**\n   - Generated configurers for components/endpoints\n   - Type-safe parameter binding\n   - Registry reference resolution (`#beanName`)\n\n---\n\n### **File Paths Summary**\n\n| Class | Path |\n|-------|------|\n| DefaultComponent | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultComponent.java` |\n| DefaultEndpoint | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultEndpoint.java` |\n| DefaultConsumer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultConsumer.java` |\n| DefaultProducer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultProducer.java` |\n| DefaultAsyncProducer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultAsyncProducer.java` |\n| PollingConsumerSupport | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/PollingConsumerSupport.java` |\n| ScheduledPollConsumer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/ScheduledPollConsumer.java` |"},{"type":"text","text":"agentId: abbf7fd (for resuming to continue this agent's work if needed)\n<usage>total_tokens: 66516\ntool_uses: 21\nduration_ms: 76611</usage>"}]}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"31d6fae3-cad3-4136-a15f-ed3562b10a42","uuid":"5a93102d-bc4d-4552-95ea-e65cd99d4bcc","tool_use_result":{"status":"completed","prompt":"Explore the Apache Camel base implementations in /workspace/core/camel-support.          lastError = null;\n                            firstPollDone = true;\n                        }\n                    }\n                } finally {\n                    pollingCounter.decrementAndGet();\n                }\n            }\n        } catch (Exception e) {\n            // Rollback strategy - may retry\n            boolean retry = (polledMessages == 0) {\n            idleCounter.incrementAndGet();\n        } else {\n            idleCounter.set(0);\n        }\n        successCounter.incrementAndGet();\n        errorCounter.set(0);\n        lastError = null;\n    }\n    \n    firstPollDone = true;\n}\n```\n\n**Abstract Methods:**\n```java\nprotected abstract int poll() throws Exception;  // Must return Component (DefaultComponent)\n   ├─ URI: \"kafka:topic?brokers=localhost:9092\"\n   └─ createEndpoint(uri, parameters)\n      ├─ Parse URI → path=\"topic\", query params\n      ├─ Validate URI syntax and parameters\n      └─ Call abstract createEndpoint(uri, path, params)\n         └─ Component implementation creates endpoint\n   \n2. Endpoint (DefaultEndpoint or subclass)\n   ├─ Stores URI, ExchangePattern, exception handling config\n   │\n   └─ When route attaches consumer:\n      ├─ createConsumer(Processor processor)\n      │  └─ Component implementation creates consumer instance\n      │     └─ Passes processor (the route/pipeline) to consumer\n      │\n      └─ When route uses producer:\n         ├─ createProducer() or createAsyncProducer()\n         └─ Returns producer wrapping any processor/executor\n\n3. Consumer (DefaultConsumer or ScheduledPollConsumer)\n   ├─ Stores:\n   │  ├─ endpoint (back-reference)\n   │  ├─ processor (the ROUTE - the pipeline to execute)\n   │  ├─ asyncProcessor (async wrapper of processor)\n   │  └─ exchangeFactory (for pooling)\n   │\n   └─ When message arrives:\n      ├─ createExchange() → uses exchangeFactory\n      ├─ endpoint.configureExchange(exchange)\n      ├─ getAsyncProcessor().process(exchange, callback)\n      │  └─ Processor (route) processes the exchange\n      └─ Callback returns exchange to pool\n\n4. Producer (DefaultProducer or DefaultAsyncProducer)\n   ├─ Stores: endpoint\n   │\n   └─ When message sent:\n      └─ process(Exchange) → Send to endpoint's target system\n\n5. ScheduledPollConsumer (extends DefaultConsumer + Runnable)\n   ├─ Same as DefaultConsumer, but:\n   │\n   ├─ Has ScheduledExecutorService\n   ├─ run() method called on schedule\n   └─ doRun() → poll() → process each message via processor\n```\n\n---\n\n### **Key Design Patterns**\n\n1. **Service Lifecycle Pattern:** All use `ServiceSupport` with `doInit/doBuild/doStart/doStop/doShutdown`\n\n2. **Async/Sync Duality:**\n   - `DefaultProducer` (sync) → `process(Exchange)`\n   - `DefaultAsyncProducer` (async) → `process(Exchange, AsyncCallback)`\n   - `AsyncProcessorConverterHelper` bridges them\n\n3. **Processor Injection:**\n   - Consumer gets Processor in constructor (the route pipeline)\n   - Processor execution handles routing/error handling\n   - Async callback returns control when done\n\n4. **Exchange Factory Pattern:**\n   - Each consumer gets dedicated `ExchangeFactory` \n   - Enables pooling/reuse of Exchange objects\n   - Per-consumer isolation\n\n5. **Strategy Pattern:**\n   - `PollingConsumerPollStrategy` for begin/commit/rollback hooks\n   - `ScheduledPollConsumerScheduler` for scheduling implementation\n   - `ExceptionHandler` for error handling\n\n6. **PropertyConfigurer Pattern:**\n   - Generated configurers for components/endpoints\n   - Type-safe parameter binding\n   - Registry reference resolution (`#beanName`)\n\n---\n\n### **File Paths Summary**\n\n| Class | Path |\n|-------|------|\n| DefaultComponent | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultComponent.java` |\n| DefaultEndpoint | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultEndpoint.java` |\n| DefaultConsumer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultConsumer.java` |\n| DefaultProducer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultProducer.java` |\n| DefaultAsyncProducer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/DefaultAsyncProducer.java` |\n| PollingConsumerSupport | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/PollingConsumerSupport.java` |\n| ScheduledPollConsumer | `/workspace/core/camel-support/src/main/java/org/apache/camel/support/ScheduledPollConsumer.java` |"}],"totalDurationMs":76611,"totalTokens":66516,"totalToolUseCount":21,"usage":{"input_tokens":0,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1313,"cache_read_input_tokens":58385,"output_tokens":6818,"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1313,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"}}}

(continues)\n│\n└── Route (runtime)\n    ├── processor = RoutePipeline\n    │   └── eventDrivenProcessors (all wrapped in Channels)\n    │       └── wrapped in InternalProcessor with UnitOfWork advice\n    │\n    ├── routePolicies\n    ├── errorHandlerFactory\n    └── properties\n```\n\n### Key Insight: Two-Phase Design\n\n1. **Design Time** (RouteDefinition)\n   - Hierarchical model of the route structure\n   - Can be introspected, modified, templated\n\n2. **Reification Time** (RouteReifier.doCreateRoute)\n   - Flattens the hierarchy into eventDrivenProcessors list\n   - Creates runtime Processors from definitions\n   - Wires in error handlers, interceptors, channels\n   - Sets up lifecycle management\n\n3. **Runtime** (Route + Processors)\n   - Consumer receives messages from endpoint\n   - Passes to RoutePipeline.process()\n   - Each Processor in chain wraps next processor in Channel\n   - Channel provides error handling, interceptors, tracing\n\n---\n\n## RouteController Role\n\n### DefaultRouteController (Facade Pattern)\n\nThe `DefaultRouteController` delegates to `InternalRouteController`:\n\n```java\nprotected RouteController getInternalRouteController() {\n    return camelContext.getCamelContextExtension().getInternalRouteController();\n}\n\n@Override\npublic void startRoute(String routeId) throws Exception {\n    getInternalRouteController().startRoute(routeId);\n}\n\n@Override\npublic void stopRoute(String routeId) throws Exception {\n    getInternalRouteController().stopRoute(routeId);\n}\n```\n\n**Responsibilities:**\n- Route lifecycle management (start/stop/suspend/resume)\n- Route status queries\n- Route group operations\n- Route reloading\n- Integration with SupervisingRouteController for fault tolerance\n\n---\n\n## Summary: Complete Flow\n\n```\n1. RouteDefinition (XML/Java DSL) → Model representation\n   \n2. Route.start() when CamelContext starts\n   ├─ Create Consumer from input endpoint\n   ├─ Consumer receives messages\n   └─ Passes to Route.processor (RoutePipeline)\n   \n4. private static boolean isStartable(Map.Entry<String, RouteService> entry) {\n   140→        boolean startable = false;\n   141→\n   142→        Consumer consumer = entry.getValue().getRoute().getConsumer();\n   143→        if (consumer instanceof SuspendableService suspendableService) {\n   144→            // consumer could be suspended, which is not reflected in\n   145→            // the BaseRouteService status\n   146→            startable = suspendableService.isSuspended();\n   147→        }\n   148→\n   149→        if (!startable && consumer instanceof entry.getValue().getStatus().isStartable();\n   156→        }\n   157→        return startable;\n   158→    }\n   159→\n   160→    /**\n   161→     * Starts the routes services in a proper manner method <b>must</b> be used to start routes in a safe manner.\n   165→     *\n   166→     * @param  checkClash     whether to check for startup order clash\n   167→     * @param  startConsumer  whether  174→    private void safelyStartRouteServices(\n   175→            AbstractCamelContext camelContext,\n   176→            boolean checkClash, boolean startConsumer, boolean resumeConsumer, boolean addingRoutes,\n   177→            Collection<RouteService> routeServices)\n   178→            throws Exception {\n   179→        lock.lock();\n   180→        try {\n   181→            // list of inputs to start when all the routes have been prepared for\n   182→            // starting\n   183→            // we use a tree map so the routes will be ordered according to startup\n   184→ started\n   188→            for (RouteService routeService : routeServices) {\n   189→                DefaultRouteStartupOrder order = doPrepareRouteToBeStarted(camelContext, routeService);\n   190→                // check for clash before we add it as input\n   191→                if (checkClash) {\n   192→                    doCheckStartupOrderClash(camelContext, order, inputs);\n   193→                }\n   194→                inputs.put(order.getStartupOrder(), order);\n   195→            }\n   196→\n   197→            // warm up routes before we start them\n   198→            doWarmUpRoutes(camelContext, inputs, startConsumer);\n   199→\n   200→            // sort the startup listeners so they are started in the right order\n   201→            camelContext.getStartupListeners().sort(OrderedComparator.get());\n   202→            // now call the startup listeners where the routes has been warmed up\n   203→            // (only the actual route consumer has not yet been started)\n   204→            for (StartupListener startup : camelContext.getStartupListeners()) {\n   205→                startup.onCamelContextStarted(camelContext.getCamelContextReference(), camelContext.isStarted());\n   206→            }\n   207→            // because the consumers may also register startup listeners we need to\n   208→            // reset\n   209→            // the already started listeners\n   210→            List<StartupListener> backup = new ArrayList<>(camelContext.getStartupListeners());\n   211→            camelContext.getStartupListeners().clear();\n   212→\n   213→            // now start the consumers\n   214→            if (startConsumer) {\n   215→                if (resumeConsumer)            doStartRouteConsumers(camelContext, inputs, addingRoutes);\n   223→                }\n   224→            }\n   225→\n   226→            // sort the startup listeners so they are started in the right order\n   227→            camelContext.getStartupListeners().sort(OrderedComparator.get());\n   228→            // now the consumers that was just started may also add new\n   229→            // StartupListeners (such as timer)\n   230→            // so we need to ensure they get started as well\n   231→            for (StartupListener startup : camelContext.getStartupListeners()) {\n   232→                startup.onCamelContextStarted(camelContext.getCamelContextReference(), camelContext.isStarted());\n   233→            }\n   234→            // and add the previous started startup listeners to the list so we have\n   235→            // them all\n   236→            camelContext.getStartupListeners().addAll(0, backup);\n   237→\n   238→            // inputs no longer needed\n   239→            inputs.clear();\n   240→        } finally {\n   241→            lock.unlock();\n   242→        }\n   243→    }\n   244→\n   245→    /**\n   246→     * @see AbstractCamelContext camelContext,\n   250→            boolean forceAutoStart, boolean checkClash, boolean startConsumer, boolean resumeConsumer, boolean addingRoutes,\n   251→ Creates `RoutePipeline` from all event-driven processors (`core/camel-core-processor/.../processor/RoutePipeline.java`)\n9. Wraps RoutePipeline in `CamelInternalProcessor` with UnitOfWork advice\n10. Adds cross-cutting advices: RoutePolicy, RouteInflightRepository, ManagementIntercept, RestBinding, Contract, Variable\n11. Creates route-level error handler and injects into all `ErrorHandlerAware` processors\n\n### Phase 3: Route Startup (Runtime Initialization)\n13. **InternalRouteStartupManager.doInitRoutes()** calls `RouteService.setUp()` (`core/camel-base-engine/.../engine/RouteService.java`)\n14. **RouteService.setUp()** calls `route.initializeServices()` → `DefaultRoute.gatherRootServices()`\n15. **DefaultRoute.gatherRootServices()** (`core/camel-base-engine/.../engine/DefaultRoute.java:685`) calls:\n    ```java\n    consumer = endpoint.createConsumer(processor);\n    ```\n    This is the critical wiring point: the route's processor chain (RoutePipeline wrapped in CamelInternalProcessor) is passed to the Endpoint, which creates a Consumer that will invoke it.\n16. **InternalRouteStartupManager.safelyStartRouteServices()** (`core/camel-base-engine/.../engine/InternalRouteStartupManager.java`):\n    - **Warmup phase:** `RouteService.warmUp()` starts the endpoint and all child services (processors, error handlers)\n    - **Listener notification:** Startup listeners notified that routes are ready\n    - **Consumer start phase:** `doStartOrResumeRouteConsumers()` calls `camelContext.startService(consumer)` — consumer begins listening\n\n### Phase 4: Message Processing (Runtime)\n17. **Consumer** receives a message from the external system (e.g., Kafka poll, HTTP request, file scan)\n18. Each processor in the chain is wrapped in a **DefaultChannel**:\n    - Channel's `getOutput()` returns the interceptor-wrapped chain\n    - Interceptors execute in declared order (outermost first)\n    - Error handler catches and handles exceptions (redelivery, dead letter)\n    - `CamelInternalProcessor` within the channel executes node-level advices\n24. For `.to()` endpoints, **SendProcessor.process()** (`core/camel-core-processor/.../processor/SendProcessor.java`):\n    - Obtains a `Producer` from the producer cache (or singleton)\n    - Calls `producer.process(exchange)` to send the message to the destination endpoint\n25. After the last processor completes, PipelineTask invokes the original callback\n26. **CamelInternalProcessor** executes after-advices in reverse order (cleanup, statistics, UoW completion)\n27. Consumer's callback handles exchange release back to the pool\n\n---\n\n## Analysis\n\n### Design Patterns Identified\n\n**1. Abstract Factory Pattern (Component → Endpoint → Consumer/Producer)**\nThe Component interface is a factory for Endpoints, and Endpoint is a factory for both Consumers and Producers. DefaultComponent parses URIs and delegates to an abstract `createEndpoint(uri, path, parameters)` method that concrete components implement. DefaultEndpoint similarly delegates `createConsumer(Processor)` and `createProducer()` to subclasses.\n\n**2. Reifier Pattern (Model-to-Runtime Bridge)**\nThe Reifier pattern separates the route model (RouteDefinition, ProcessorDefinition hierarchy) from the runtime execution objects (Route, Processor chain). `ProcessorReifier` maintains a registry mapping each `ProcessorDefinition` subclass to its corresponding reifier (e.g., `ToDefinition` → `SendReifier`, `FilterDefinition` → `FilterReifier`). This clean separation enables multiple DSLs (Java, XML, YAML) to share the same runtime engine, and allows the model to be introspected, serialized, or modified before reification.\n\n**3. Chain of Responsibility (Pipeline + Channel)**\nThe Pipeline processor chains multiple processors sequentially, passing each exchange through them in order. Each processor in the chain is wrapped in a Channel that adds interceptors and error handling. The PipelineHelper determines whether processing should continue based on exchange state (failure, rollback, routeStop).\n\n**4. Decorator Pattern (Channel Interceptor Wrapping)**\nDefaultChannel wraps each processor with multiple layers of interceptors. During `initChannel()`, interceptors are reversed and applied in sequence, creating an onion-like layering where the first-declared interceptor is outermost (executed first). The error handler wraps all interceptors as the outermost layer. This creates a structure:\n```\nErrorHandler → InterceptorN → ... → Interceptor1 → NextProcessor\n```\n\n**5. Advice Pattern (CamelInternalProcessor)**\nCamelInternalProcessor uses a before/after advice pattern for cross-cutting concerns. Each `CamelInternalProcessorAdvice` provides `before(exchange)` returning state, and `after(exchange, state)` for cleanup. Advices execute before in declaration order and after in reverse order. This handles UnitOfWork lifecycle, RoutePolicy callbacks, JMX statistics, tracing, message history, and stream caching without deep call stacks.\n\n**6. Callback Continuation (Async Processing Model)**\nRather than blocking threads, Camel uses `AsyncCallback` for non-blocking processing. `AsyncProcessor.process(Exchange, AsyncCallback)` returns `true` for synchronous completion or `false` for asynchronous, with the callback invoked later. Pipeline's `PipelineTask` implements `AsyncCallback` itself, chaining processors by passing itself as the callback — when one processor completes, the task reschedules itself for the next processor via the `ReactiveExecutor`.\n\n**7. Object Pooling (Exchange and Task Pooling)**\nExchanges are created via per-consumer `ExchangeFactory` instances that support pooling for reduced GC pressure. Pipeline tasks implement `PooledExchangeTask` with `prepare()/reset()` methods for reuse. The `ReactiveExecutor` manages scheduling of these pooled tasks.\n\n**8. Strategy Pattern (Pluggable Behaviors)**\nMultiple pluggable strategy interfaces allow customization: `InterceptStrategy` for processor wrapping, `PollingConsumerPollStrategy` for poll lifecycle (begin/commit/rollback), `ScheduledPollConsumerScheduler` for scheduling, `ErrorHandlerFactory` for error handling, and `RoutePolicy` for lifecycle callbacks.\n\n**9. Two-Phase Startup (Processors Before Consumers)**\nRoute startup carefully separates processor initialization from consumer activation. During warmup, all processors, error handlers, and services are started. Only after all processors are confirmed ready does the startup manager start the consumers. This prevents race conditions where messages arrive before the processing chain is fully initialized.\n\n### Component Responsibilities\n\n| Component | Responsibility |\n|-----------|---------------|\n| **Component** | URI parsing, Endpoint factory, component-level configuration |\n| **Endpoint** | Message endpoint abstraction, Consumer/Producer/Exchange factory |\n| **Consumer** | Message reception from external system, Exchange creation, Processor invocation |\n| **Producer** | Message delivery to external system, Exchange processing |\n| **Processor** | Core processing unit; transforms, routes, or mediates Exchanges |\n| **Exchange** | Message container with IN/OUT messages, properties, exception state |\n| **Pipeline** | Sequential processor chaining with async callback continuation |\n| **RoutePipeline** | Marker subclass identifying the root of a route's processor chain |\n| **Channel** | Interceptor/error-handler wrapper around each processor node |\n| **CamelInternalProcessor** | Cross-cutting advice executor (UoW, tracing, policies, stats) |\n| **RouteReifier** | Converts RouteDefinition model to runtime Route with full processor chain |\n| **ProcessorReifier** | Maps ProcessorDefinition subclasses to runtime Processor instances |\n| **DefaultRoute** | Runtime route holder; creates Consumer from Endpoint + Processor during init |\n| **RouteService** | Orchestrates route lifecycle phases: setUp → warmUp → start |\n| **InternalRouteStartupManager** | Coordinates safe, ordered startup across all routes |\n| **SendProcessor** | Handles `.to()` by obtaining and invoking a Producer on the destination endpoint |\n\n### Data Flow Description\n\nA message enters Camel through a **Consumer** that is listening on an input **Endpoint**. The Consumer creates an **Exchange** (potentially from a pool) containing the inbound **Message** and invokes its **AsyncProcessor** — which is the route's processor chain.\n\nThe exchange first passes through **CamelInternalProcessor** which executes before-advices: creating a **UnitOfWork** (transaction boundary), notifying **RoutePolicies**, registering with the **InflightRepository**, and enabling tracing/message history.\n\nThe exchange then enters the **RoutePipeline**, which schedules a **PipelineTask** on the **ReactiveExecutor**. The task iterates through processors sequentially. For each step, it calls `prepareOutToIn()` to promote the OUT message to IN, then invokes the next processor.\n\nEach processor node is wrapped in a **DefaultChannel** that applies interceptors (in declared order) and an error handler (outermost). Within the Channel, another **CamelInternalProcessor** handles node-level advices (debugging, backlog tracing, per-node statistics).\n\nWhen the exchange reaches a **SendProcessor** (`.to()` node), the processor obtains a **Producer** from its cache and calls `producer.process(exchange)`, which delivers the message to the destination endpoint.\n\nIf any processor fails, the error handler within the Channel catches the exception and may perform redelivery, route to a dead letter channel, or propagate the failure. `PipelineHelper.continueProcessing()` checks failure/rollback/routeStop flags after each step to determine whether the pipeline should continue.\n\nAfter the last processor completes, the PipelineTask invokes the original callback, which triggers **CamelInternalProcessor** after-advices in reverse order (cleanup, statistics collection, UoW completion). The exchange is then released back to the Consumer's pool.\n\n### Interface Contracts Between Components\n\n- **Component → Endpoint:** `Component.createEndpoint(uri)` returns a fully configured Endpoint. The Component handles URI parsing, parameter extraction, and property binding.\n- **Endpoint → Consumer:** `Endpoint.createConsumer(Processor)` returns a Consumer that will invoke the given Processor for each received message. The Processor is the route's pipeline.\n- **Endpoint → Producer:** `Endpoint.createProducer()` returns a Producer that can send Exchanges to the endpoint's destination.\n- **Consumer → Processor:** Consumer holds a reference to the route Processor (passed at construction) and calls `processor.process(exchange, callback)` for each message.\n- **Pipeline → Processor[]:** Pipeline holds an ordered list of AsyncProcessors and chains them via callback continuation. Each processor must call the callback when done.\n- **Channel → Processor:** Channel wraps a single next-processor with interceptors and error handler. `Channel.getOutput()` returns the fully wrapped chain. `Channel.getNextProcessor()` returns the unwrapped inner processor.\n- **RouteReifier → Route:** RouteReifier creates the Route, builds the processor chain from the definition, and sets `route.setProcessor(chain)`. The Route holds this processor until `gatherRootServices()` passes it to `endpoint.createConsumer(processor)`.\n- **ProcessorReifier → Processor:** Each ProcessorReifier subclass creates a specific runtime Processor from its corresponding ProcessorDefinition, then wraps it in a Channel.\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\nApache Camel routes messages through a layered architecture where **Components** create **Endpoints**, which in turn create **Consumers** (for receiving) and **Producers** (for sending). The **RouteReifier** bridges the DSL model (`RouteDefinition` → `ProcessorDefinition` tree) to the runtime by recursively reifying each definition node into a runtime **Processor**, wrapping each in a **DefaultChannel** (which layers interceptors, error handlers, and cross-cutting advices via **CamelInternalProcessor**), and assembling them into a **RoutePipeline** that chains processors via async callback continuation. At startup, `DefaultRoute.gatherRootServices()` wires the complete processor chain to the Consumer via `endpoint.createConsumer(processor)`, with a two-phase startup ensuring all processors are initialized before the Consumer begins listening — creating a fully assembled, non-blocking routing engine that processes Exchanges through the complete Component→Endpoint→Consumer→Processor→Producer hierarchy.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":120,"cache_read_input_tokens":49374,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":120},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"31d6fae3-cad3-4136-a15f-ed3562b10a42","uuid":"0b9b9c15-a0fd-4b3c-88e6-e05595444642"}

Creates route-level error handler and injects into all `ErrorHandlerAware` processors\n\n### Phase 3: Route Startup (Runtime Initialization)\n13. **InternalRouteStartupManager.doInitRoutes()** calls `RouteService.setUp()` (`core/camel-base-engine/.../engine/RouteService.java`)\n14. **RouteService.setUp()** calls `route.initializeServices()` → `DefaultRoute.gatherRootServices()`\n15. **DefaultRoute.gatherRootServices()** (`core/camel-base-engine/.../engine/DefaultRoute.java:685`) calls:\n    ```java\n    consumer = endpoint.createConsumer(processor);\n    ```\n    This is the critical wiring point: the route's processor chain (RoutePipeline wrapped in CamelInternalProcessor) is passed to the Endpoint, which creates a Consumer that will invoke it.\n16. **InternalRouteStartupManager.safelyStartRouteServices()** (`core/camel-base-engine/.../engine/InternalRouteStartupManager.java`):\n    - **Warmup phase:** `RouteService.warmUp()` starts the endpoint and all child services (processors, error handlers)\n    - **Listener notification:** Startup listeners notified that routes are ready\n    - **Consumer start phase:** `doStartOrResumeRouteConsumers()` calls `camelContext.startService(consumer)` — consumer begins listening\n\n### Phase 4: Message Processing (Runtime)\n17. **Consumer** receives a message from the external system (e.g., Kafka poll, HTTP request, file scan)\n18. Consumer calls `createExchange()` via its `ExchangeFactory` (pooled), then `endpoint.configureExchange(exchange)`\n19. Consumer invokes `getAsyncProcessor().process(exchange, callback)` — this is the route's processor chain\n20. **CamelInternalProcessor.process()** executes before-advices (UnitOfWork, RoutePolicy, tracing, message history, stream caching)\n21. Delegates to **RoutePipeline.process()** which creates a `PipelineTask` and schedules it on the `ReactiveExecutor`\n22. **PipelineTask.run()** iterates through processors:\n    - Checks stop conditions via `PipelineHelper.continueProcessing()` (failed, rollback, routeStop)\n    - Calls `ExchangeHelper.prepareOutToIn(exchange)` — converts OUT message to IN for next processor\n    - Invokes `processors.get(index++).process(exchange, this)` — passes itself as callback\n    - On callback completion, reschedules itself for next processor\n23. Each processor in the chain is wrapped in a **DefaultChannel**:\n    - Channel's `getOutput()` returns the interceptor-wrapped chain\n    - Interceptors execute in declared order (outermost first)\n    - Error handler catches and handles exceptions (redelivery, dead letter)\n    - `CamelInternalProcessor` within the channel executes node-level advices\n24. For `.to()` endpoints, **SendProcessor.process()** (`core/camel-core-processor/.../processor/SendProcessor.java`):\n    - Obtains a `Producer` from the producer cache (or singleton)\n    - Calls `producer.process(exchange)` to send the message to the destination endpoint\n25. After the last processor completes, PipelineTask invokes the original callback\n26. **CamelInternalProcessor** executes after-advices in reverse order (cleanup, statistics, UoW completion)\n27. Consumer's callback handles exchange release back to the pool\n\n---\n\n## Analysis\n\n### Design Patterns Identified\n\n**1. Abstract Factory Pattern (Component → Endpoint → Consumer/Producer)**\nThe Component interface is a factory for Endpoints, and Endpoint is a factory for both Consumers and Producers. DefaultComponent parses URIs and delegates to an abstract `createEndpoint(uri, path, parameters)` method that concrete components implement. DefaultEndpoint similarly delegates `createConsumer(Processor)` and `createProducer()` to subclasses.\n\n**2. Reifier Pattern (Model-to-Runtime Bridge)**\nThe Reifier pattern separates the route model (RouteDefinition, ProcessorDefinition hierarchy) from the runtime execution objects (Route, Processor chain). `ProcessorReifier` maintains a registry mapping each `ProcessorDefinition` subclass to its corresponding reifier (e.g., `ToDefinition` → `SendReifier`, `FilterDefinition` → `FilterReifier`). This clean separation enables multiple DSLs (Java, XML, YAML) to share the same runtime engine, and allows the model to be introspected, serialized, or modified before reification.\n\n**3. Chain of Responsibility (Pipeline + Channel)**\nThe Pipeline processor chains multiple processors sequentially, passing each exchange through them in order. Each processor in the chain is wrapped in a Channel that adds interceptors and error handling. The PipelineHelper determines whether processing should continue based on exchange state (failure, rollback, routeStop).\n\n**4. Decorator Pattern (Channel Interceptor Wrapping)**\nDefaultChannel wraps each processor with multiple layers of interceptors. During `initChannel()`, interceptors are reversed and applied in sequence, creating an onion-like layering where the first-declared interceptor is outermost (executed first). The error handler wraps all interceptors as the outermost layer. This creates a structure:\n```\nErrorHandler → InterceptorN → ... → Interceptor1 → NextProcessor\n```\n\n**5. Advice Pattern (CamelInternalProcessor)**\nCamelInternalProcessor uses a before/after advice pattern for cross-cutting concerns. Each `CamelInternalProcessorAdvice` provides `before(exchange)` returning state, and `after(exchange, state)` for cleanup. Advices execute before in declaration order and after in reverse order. This handles UnitOfWork lifecycle, RoutePolicy callbacks, JMX statistics, tracing, message history, and stream caching without deep call stacks.\n\n**6. Callback Continuation (Async Processing Model)**\nRather than blocking threads, Camel uses `AsyncCallback` for non-blocking processing. `AsyncProcessor.process(Exchange, AsyncCallback)` returns `true` for synchronous completion or `false` for asynchronous, with the callback invoked later. Pipeline's `PipelineTask` implements `AsyncCallback` itself, chaining processors by passing itself as the callback — when one processor completes, the task reschedules itself for the next processor via the `ReactiveExecutor`.\n\n**7. Object Pooling (Exchange and Task Pooling)**\nExchanges are created via per-consumer `ExchangeFactory` instances that support pooling for reduced GC pressure. Pipeline tasks implement `PooledExchangeTask` with `prepare()/reset()` methods for reuse. The `ReactiveExecutor` manages scheduling of these pooled tasks.\n\n**8. Strategy Pattern (Pluggable Behaviors)**\nMultiple pluggable strategy interfaces allow customization: `InterceptStrategy` for processor wrapping, `PollingConsumerPollStrategy` for poll lifecycle (begin/commit/rollback), `ScheduledPollConsumerScheduler` for scheduling, `ErrorHandlerFactory` for error handling, and `RoutePolicy` for lifecycle callbacks.\n\n**9. Two-Phase Startup (Processors Before Consumers)**\nRoute startup carefully separates processor initialization from consumer activation. During warmup, all processors, error handlers, and services are started. Only after all processors are confirmed ready does the startup manager start the consumers. This prevents race conditions where messages arrive before the processing chain is fully initialized.\n\n### Component Responsibilities\n\n| Component | Responsibility |\n|-----------|---------------|\n| **Component** | URI parsing, Endpoint factory, component-level configuration |\n| **Endpoint** | Message endpoint abstraction, Consumer/Producer/Exchange factory |\n| **Consumer** | Message reception from external system, Exchange creation, Processor invocation |\n| **Producer** | Message delivery to external system, Exchange processing |\n| **Processor** | Core processing unit; transforms, routes, or mediates Exchanges |\n| **Exchange** | Message container with IN/OUT messages, properties, exception state |\n| **Pipeline** | Sequential processor chaining with async callback continuation |\n| **RoutePipeline** | Marker subclass identifying the root of a route's processor chain |\n| **Channel** | Interceptor/error-handler wrapper around each processor node |\n| **CamelInternalProcessor** | Cross-cutting advice executor (UoW, tracing, policies, stats) |\n| **RouteReifier** | Converts RouteDefinition model to runtime Route with full processor chain |\n| **ProcessorReifier** | Maps ProcessorDefinition subclasses to runtime Processor instances |\n| **DefaultRoute** | Runtime route holder; creates Consumer from Endpoint + Processor during init |\n| **RouteService** | Orchestrates route lifecycle phases: setUp → warmUp → start |\n| **InternalRouteStartupManager** | Coordinates safe, ordered startup across all routes |\n| **SendProcessor** | Handles `.to()` by obtaining and invoking a Producer on the destination endpoint |\n\n### Data Flow Description\n\nA message enters Camel through a **Consumer** that is listening on an input **Endpoint**. The Consumer creates an **Exchange** (potentially from a pool) containing the inbound **Message** and invokes its **AsyncProcessor** — which is the route's processor chain.\n\nThe exchange first passes through **CamelInternalProcessor** which executes before-advices: creating a **UnitOfWork** (transaction boundary), notifying **RoutePolicies**, registering with the **InflightRepository**, and enabling tracing/message history.\n\nThe exchange then enters the **RoutePipeline**, which schedules a **PipelineTask** on the **ReactiveExecutor**. The task iterates through processors sequentially. For each step, it calls `prepareOutToIn()` to promote the OUT message to IN, then invokes the next processor.\n\nEach processor node is wrapped in a **DefaultChannel** that applies interceptors (in declared order) and an error handler (outermost). Within the Channel, another **CamelInternalProcessor** handles node-level advices (debugging, backlog tracing, per-node statistics).\n\nWhen the exchange reaches a **SendProcessor** (`.to()` node), the processor obtains a **Producer** from its cache and calls `producer.process(exchange)`, which delivers the message to the destination endpoint.\n\nIf any processor fails, the error handler within the Channel catches the exception and may perform redelivery, route to a dead letter channel, or propagate the failure. `PipelineHelper.continueProcessing()` checks failure/rollback/routeStop flags after each step to determine whether the pipeline should continue.\n\nAfter the last processor completes, the PipelineTask invokes the original callback, which triggers **CamelInternalProcessor** after-advices in reverse order (cleanup, statistics collection, UoW completion). The exchange is then released back to the Consumer's pool.\n\n### Interface Contracts Between Components\n\n- **Component → Endpoint:** `Component.createEndpoint(uri)` returns a fully configured Endpoint. The Component handles URI parsing, parameter extraction, and property binding.\n- **Endpoint → Consumer:** `Endpoint.createConsumer(Processor)` returns a Consumer that will invoke the given Processor for each received message. The Processor is the route's pipeline.\n- **Endpoint → Producer:** `Endpoint.createProducer()` returns a Producer that can send Exchanges to the endpoint's destination.\n- **Consumer → Processor:** Consumer holds a reference to the route Processor (passed at construction) and calls `processor.process(exchange, callback)` for each message.\n- **Pipeline → Processor[]:** Pipeline holds an ordered list of AsyncProcessors and chains them via callback continuation. Each processor must call the callback when done.\n- **Channel → Processor:** Channel wraps a single next-processor with interceptors and error handler. `Channel.getOutput()` returns the fully wrapped chain. `Channel.getNextProcessor()` returns the unwrapped inner processor.\n- **RouteReifier → Route:** RouteReifier creates the Route, builds the processor chain from the definition, and sets `route.setProcessor(chain)`. The Route holds this processor until `gatherRootServices()` passes it to `endpoint.createConsumer(processor)`.\n- **ProcessorReifier → Processor:** Each ProcessorReifier subclass creates a specific runtime Processor from its corresponding ProcessorDefinition, then wraps it in a Channel.\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\nApache Camel routes messages through a layered architecture where **Components** create **Endpoints**, which in turn create **Consumers** (for receiving) and **Producers** (for sending). The **RouteReifier** bridges the DSL model (`RouteDefinition` → `ProcessorDefinition` tree) to the runtime by recursively reifying each definition node into a runtime **Processor**, wrapping each in a **DefaultChannel** (which layers interceptors, error handlers, and cross-cutting advices via **CamelInternalProcessor**), and assembling them into a **RoutePipeline** that chains processors via async callback continuation. At startup, `DefaultRoute.gatherRootServices()` wires the complete processor chain to the Consumer via `endpoint.createConsumer(processor)`, with a two-phase startup ensuring all processors are initialized before the Consumer begins listening — creating a fully assembled, non-blocking routing engine that processes Exchanges through the complete Component→Endpoint→Consumer→Processor→Producer hierarchy.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
